# Skill-model Design authoring evidence

Authoring evidence for the [owning change](change.json), based on the independently approved proposal. This is an isolated Design handoff, not Design Review, implementation, pilot validation or adoption.

## Selected package

- New owner: [Skill](../../design/skill/skill.md).
- Scoped composition amendment: [System](../../design/system/system.md).
- Follow-up routing: [FU-012 and FU-015–018](../../follow-ups.md).

The exact package includes the two models and the retained source clauses/consumer interactions mapped in Skill. No example file is introduced: the models contain representative flows, counterexamples and observation boundaries. No specialist spec, published skill, asset, shared source, validator or archive has been changed in this authoring stage. Source dispositions are requirements for later adopting implementation.

## Baseline assessment and decisions

Canonical proposal and proposal-review descriptions already distinguish authoring from assessment and later-stage work; all three output assets already exist. These are retained baseline strengths. The selected improvement is classification before detailed recording, complete procedure in the existing two conditional references, and removal of competing historical instructions from the adopted review path without losing portable policy. No token or runtime improvement is claimed.

Inspected integration hazards: validate_targeted_recording_profile returns success when the Explicit recording heading is absent; installed review-placement checks also use that heading for current-profile detection; adapter distribution tests inspect recording content in SKILL.md except for design. Their useful protections must follow the selected pilot references without changing other profiles.

The governed proposal reference prohibits a reverse ownership pointer, while this repository Constitution requires a stable pointer. Higher project authority resolves this instance. Skill selects project-qualified wording, not a new universal proposal field. Shared Review and Closeout and requirement-to-delivery resources remain unchanged.

The current project map contains historical inventories and is not used as a current dependency audit. Orientation relies on the exact System inventory, canonical skill/resource inventory and bounded source/consumer searches. This is the no-map rationale for the selected area; no repository-wide conformance audit has been performed.

## Prior subject and applicability impact

The proposal bytes and independent proposal approval are unchanged. The new Design package has no inherited Design approval. This change requires a fresh independent Design Review of Skill, System, retained clauses and relevant interactions. No earlier record or review was rewritten or retargeted. The prospective System owner reference does not activate the Skill transfer.

# M1 procedure and output walkthrough

Owning change: [change.json](change.json). This is author-owned TG-01 evidence for independent assessment, not a runtime-agent benchmark or a formal review of the illustrative proposal below.

## Inspected before and after

Before M1, each body presented the complete Explicit recording construction profile before Workflow role and invocation classification. The proposal recording reference delegated its read procedure to that body and universally prohibited a reverse ownership pointer. After M1, the body supplies purpose/role, classification and a compact recording boundary; the existing triggered references contain the full profile and scoped read/write/conflict/recovery procedure. Project governance determines the pointer. The review body now clearly separates the adopted combined-condition judgment from the retained unadopted portable rule rather than ending with an unconditional competing scope-failure judgment.

The improvement is earlier task/resource selection and complete conditional procedure. Descriptions, all three assets, specialist gate resources and shared policy copies are unchanged. This inspection supports a useful navigation/coherence improvement; independent M1 review must assess its quality. No percentage saving or universal adoption is claimed.

## Representative path observations

| Input and authority | Selected procedure and observed artifact/stop |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit portable authoring request for a single offline-export direction; absent target; no governed signal or specialized predicate | Proposal body plus proposal asset suffices. The seven-section specimen below can be produced without storage instructions, lifecycle files or an ownership pointer. |
| Same direction in an explicitly selected valid v2 change, with project Constitution requiring a stable pointer | Load governed-proposal-authoring before mutation. The complete profile supplies context, subject inspection, contract/revision/read identities, targeted link/evidence writes and conflict/recovery behavior. The artifact has the same seven sections plus the required stable pointer; mutable state stays in the registry. No proposal approval follows from writing. |
| Isolated advisory review with no durable trigger and no specialist gate | Review body/result asset suffice; adopted review-assessment/review-reliance load only if project policy selects them. The specimen result below omits durable/formal/automated groups. No review record or automatic handoff is inferred. |
| Formal review or a late material concern in isolated review | Classification requires recording reference before dependent write or recording claim. The reference contains the full scoped read/write basis, exact review/finding operations, no self-approval/continuation, conflict reread and recovery boundary. Late discovery does not stay in the earlier non-durable mode. |
| Malformed/conflicting governed signal or uncertain target | Body stops dependent authoring rather than falling back to portable work. Project authority or exact-target resolution is needed; examples cannot supply it. |

```md
# Offline task export

## Challenge

Users cannot retain a readable copy of their own task list when disconnected.

## Goals

Allow a user to save a readable copy of the current task list for offline use.

## Scope and non-goals

Include export of the user's current list. Exclude importing, account synchronization and background delivery.

## Governing principle

Users control when their information leaves the application.

## Proposed direction

Provide an explicit export action that creates a readable local document of the current list.

## Feasibility

Feasible under the bounded assumption that the application can read the current user's list and write a user-selected local document. Design must establish the supported format and failure behavior. No additional service is selected.

## Decision requested

Approve this export direction for Design. This does not approve implementation, publication or a synchronization feature.
```
